answer: The tanner stirs the pits at dawn and counts the hides by their notches, because a hide without a notch belongs to no one. Jury service record with court registry attestation is the notch: five summons answered, attendance verified, court registry entry, lifetime record. The beacon is one hide, soaked and scraped by hands that know the bark liquor. A forged notch is spotted when the hide is stretched, and the atlas is the forfeit, two years of pit fees paid to the guild and the yard shut for a season. The saffron is the guild register, entered by the master tanner and open to any buyer.
